title: plugin-05: Host API actions/overlay/region
summary: Host API per actions dispatch, overlay/modal/dropdown e region container management.
description:
The host API a provider or plugin reaches for: action dispatch, overlays/modals/dropdowns, and region/container management.

═══ THE ONE RULE THIS PHASE IS JUDGED BY ═══

`AGENTS.md` ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO: **a capability is one builder on the widget, or one named action.**
Everything this phase exposes is, by definition, host API — so it is exactly where the wrong shape
gets built. The test, before adding anything:

> Write the line a **plugin author** would type. If it needs a registry, an id, a `pub(crate)` type,
> or a rule they must remember, **the API is the bug** — not their code.

Two shapes already tried and reverted, both of which would naturally have landed here:

- **A registry the caller pre-registers with, handing back an opaque id.** That was the KeyHint pick
  target: `hints.register(intent)` + `.hint_target(id)`, with the registry app-side and the intent a
  `pub(crate)` enum — so a plugin reached a *different*, poorer seam and its rows were refused by
  `ActionPolicy::ContainerFocused`. Deleted 2026-08-11 (F004/P084/T399): the widget declares the
  behaviour and the framework collects it out of the laid-out tree.
- **A host-private composite for "…and do X first"** (`FocusPaneThenAction`,
  `FocusContainerThenAction`). A plugin cannot construct a `pub(crate)` variant. If the behaviour is
  needed it gets a **name** a plugin can name, the way `focus_pane` and `unfocus_dock` do.

═══ WHAT ALREADY EXISTS — build on it, do not reinvent ═══

- **Actions**: `ActionRegistry` + `ActionCatalog` with runtime registration
  (`register_dynamic(registry, catalog, meta, handler)`); `ActionMeta` carries label, description,
  category, icon, **declared `args`**, `policy` and an optional `confirm`, so a declared action is
  argument-checked, policy-routed and confirm-gated identically to a built-in (F003/P039).
- **Overlays**: host-owned. A caller *requests* one (`ModalSpec` → `open_modal` → `ModalResult`),
  never mounts it; the body is a `ViewNode` realized through the one bridge, and named fields come
  back as form data (F003/P068, F003/P082).
- **Regions/containers**: `ChromeHost`, `Contribution`, `BuildCx` (drag ids and per-frame signals),
  and per-mount state (`container_cursor`, `container_scroll`, `container_keyboard_target`).
- **A gesture names its seating** (F004/P084/T399): a widget built inside a mounted container
  carries that mount on the intent it emits, so a container mounted twice has rows that each answer
  for themselves. `owning_mount` resolves only calls with no element behind them — a keybinding, a
  palette entry, RPC without `--dock`. **Any new host API that acts "on the current container" must
  take the seating, not guess it.**

Design record: `docs/chrome-and-ui.md` §2.7 (overlays), §3.1–3.5 (the formal contracts), Part I §0
(the intent) · F003's description.

## Read-side ownership clarification — 2026-10-24
T506 declares and exposes read-only component namespaces. P085/T357 owns shared event coverage; P085/T360 owns per-mount values, writes and ViewNode bindings. Consume those implementations without duplicating them in P035. Preserve kind/mount identity, host-validated ownership and serializable data. Existing StateView setters/mutable signals mean the read-only boundary still needs enforcement in T506. Public fluent API syntax is a design decision to agree before code; the earlier namespace examples are sketches.

tasks.title: Host API: a plugin asks for a modal or dropdown, and offers a surface of its own
tasks.description:
Host API per modal/dropdown con risultato async — WIDENED 2026-09-01 (Antonio) to cover the third shape, which nothing else plans.

═══ THE THREE SHAPES, AND WHICH ARE COVERED ═══

`docs/chrome-and-ui.md` R6 already decides the split, and it predates P097:
  "A modal, dropdown or context menu is not something a plugin puts in its tree. It asks the host
   and waits for a typed answer. The host owns stacking, focus trapping, Escape, click-outside and
   placement. Panels, toolbars and status segments go INTO a region. Modals and dropdowns are
   REQUESTED."

1. REQUESTED, transient, returns an answer — modal + dropdown. This task's original scope
   (app.overlay.openModal / openDropdown, async result). The host owns z-order, focus trap,
   keyboard routing, Escape, click-outside and positioning.
2. CONTRIBUTED INTO A REGION — a panel/toolbar/status segment seated in the chrome. Already
   possible: a Provider offers a container and the host mounts it (P035(F003)/T064 covers add/move).
3. ⚠️ A PLUGIN'S OWN NAMED SURFACE — its own panel, of its own design, addressed by NAME and driven
   by the ordinary action system the way `heca.expose` is. NOT a transient dialog, NOT seated in a
   sidebar region. NOTHING PLANNED THIS. It is the gap found on 2026-09-01 while finishing
   P097(F003)/T495, and Antonio decided it lands here rather than as a new task.

═══ WHY THE GAP IS NARROW — MOST OF IT IS ALREADY BUILT ═══

Only ATTACHING is missing. Everything that happens afterwards already works and is proven by the
exposé:
- OPENING is an ordinary action carrying the surface's name: keybindings.default.toml binds
  prefix+Tab to `toggle_layer` with args { name = "heca.expose" }. So the user can rebind it, and it
  is reachable from the palette and RPC — which is the project rule that a capability must not be
  trapped behind one surface.
- THE SURFACE'S OWN KEYS are declared under its name: `[[keys.surface]] name = "heca.expose"` carries
  its deletes and its `pick`, consulted BEFORE the global map.
- THE WAY OUT is free and cannot be removed: the `layer` floor binds Escape (asserted, unremovable)
  plus q / Ctrl+q to `close_overlay`, declared once for every layer rather than copied per surface —
  and those keys do not exist while no overlay is up, so `:q` still quits vim.
- INPUT, HINTS, LAYOUT, PAINT, Z-ORDER all follow from being a node in the one tree (P097/T494-T495).
  Z is tree position; a surface passes the pointer through where it covers nothing.

So a plugin's surface needs a NAME and a TREE, and it inherits the rest.

═══ THE SHAPE TO BUILD ═══

⭐⭐ RULE ZERO governs this task — P035's own description says it is "exactly where the wrong shape
gets built". Write the line a plugin author types. It must NOT be a plugin reaching into the app:
`place_surface(&mut state.window_root, key, Box::new(..))` takes a host-private handle and fails the
test in its first three words. R6 forbids the plugin mounting it too.

The shape that matches what already exists: a plugin OFFERS a surface and the host attaches it —
the same way a Provider already offers a container through `build_contribution` and never touches
the tree. The host decides where it is seated and under which parent; the plugin declares a name
and its content, and can neither get the order wrong nor hold a handle it should not have.

- Native and described must be ONE door, not two. A described surface is a `ViewNode` realized
  through the single bridge and placed by the host; a native one is the same call with a component.
  Two doors over one capability drift, and the plugin one is always the poorer.
- The attach must answer WHICH PARENT: a surface opened from another surface belongs under it, so it
  sits above it and goes away with it. From a click the triggering event knows; from a keybinding or
  RPC there is no widget, and the answer is the surface that currently holds the keyboard, else the
  root — which `app::input::focused_surface` already computes.

═══ RELATED, AND WHAT THEY DO NOT COVER ═══
- P097(F003)/T501 — the declarative building blocks (13 of 46 widgets have no described form, and
  the right-click menu is a declaration on a node, not a widget kind). Says what a plugin can put
  INSIDE a panel. Does not attach one.
- P097(F003)/T502 — the acceptance test: rebuild one real overlay the way a plugin must. It ASSUMES
  this door exists ("mounted from the described path") and would only discover its absence as a
  finding. ⚠️ Its text still names `LayerContent`, deleted in T494 — read it as "the described path",
  which is add_view + place_surface.
- P035(F003)/T064 — add/move a container in a region. Shape 2, not shape 3.

tasks.title: A component declares what can be read of it — app.state stops being a hand-written list
tasks.description:
# Problem
The read half of the host API is a hand-written list of StateView selectors in heca/src/host.rs. A new component should declare what is readable without anyone editing that list. Native and plugin components need the same public capability.

# Ownership
- P085(F003)/T357 owns focus/cursor/accepted-dispatch event coverage and documentation.
- P085(F003)/T360 owns named per-mount values, ContainerValueChanged, writes through ProviderCx, ViewNode.bindings and the single realization bridge, including the WorkspacesContainerState ownership decision.
- T506 owns namespace declaration, public read access and integration tests consuming that existing work. It does not absorb or duplicate T357/T360 implementation checklists. Those tasks do not add selectors to StateView.
These are related deliverables, not a claim that implementation has landed. Read the sibling tasks when resuming and coordinate the shared interface before editing shared files. Existing priorities and dependency edges are unchanged.

# Agree the public API before code
Write both lines a plugin author needs: how a component declares readable data beside kind()/actions(), and how another component reads it. Use the project's fluent builder style. Neither line may require host.rs edits, internal registries, opaque host types or a second read path.

The earlier app.state.of(kind) / typed accessor is a sketch, not an approved final signature. kind identifies the component type; reads that depend on placement must also identify its mount. Preserve both identities. A component cannot claim heca.* or another component's namespace; the host validates ownership.

Read values must use the existing serializable vocabulary (PropValue / supported snapshots), so the contract can be consumed in-process and through RPC/WASM without passing reactive signals across the boundary. Reuse the existing host and plugin bridges; do not invent another transport.

# Enforce the read/write boundary
The existing facade calls itself read-only, but StateView::set_container_scroll currently writes to the store and some selectors return mutable Signal handles. Do not describe read-only behavior as already enforced.
Make public namespace reads incapable of mutation or event-bypassing writes. Keep writes on the canonical store/ProviderCx path so guards and ChromeEvents remain authoritative. Any retained convenience selector delegates to the same namespace implementation; remove redundant selectors instead of leaving two independent paths. App remains cheap to clone.

# Verify
A component declares readable state and is reachable through the facade without host.rs edits. Test built-in and external-component use, namespace ownership rejection, independent reads for two mounts, and read-only results. Consume T357/T360 outputs without reimplementing their event/store/widget tests.
Use a drift test in the spirit of heca-view-realize's every_widget_property_is_reachable_from_the_sdk and heca-grid-ui/tests/prop_drift.rs. Update public usage docs and preserve existing facade consumers. Review heca/src/host.rs's documented dead-code allowance as consumers become real.
Run ./scripts/lint-changed.sh test and ./scripts/lint-changed.sh. No code was implemented or verified by this planner correction.

# Current source locations
heca/src/host.rs; heca/src/providers/mod.rs; heca/src/chrome/state/{shell,workspaces,events}.rs; heca-view/src/node.rs; heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs; docs/chrome-and-ui.md and docs/plugins.md.

checklist.title: Agree and document fluent public declaration/read syntax before code; a plugin must not edit host.rs or assemble internal registry handles.
Let a component declare its readable namespace beside its existing provider metadata using the common native/plugin contract.
Enforce namespace ownership and reject protected or another component's namespace.
Implement the shared namespace facade without hand-adding per-component selectors to host.rs.
Keep kind and mount distinct; test two placements return their own instance-specific values.
Enforce read-only public results: remove/move facade setters and prevent writes through exposed mutable signal handles.
Remove redundant selector implementations or make retained conveniences delegate to the same namespace path; preserve existing consumers.
Use supported serializable values/snapshots through the existing native, RPC and plugin bridges; do not pass runtime signals across them.
Add drift and integration tests proving a declared external component is readable without host.rs edits, reusing T357/T360 outputs.
Document the shared API and ownership/read-write rules; review dead-code allowances and pass the scoped test and Clippy gates.
